record.paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For each integer r at least 6, does there exist a constant c prime depending only on r such that, for every number of edges m, there is a graph with m edges and girth r whose largest bipartite subgraph has no more than m/2 + c prime m^(r/(r+1)) edges?

evidence.quote:

artifact.category_tag: extremal graph theory: max-cut and girth
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, due to Bollobás and Scott, strengthens an earlier conjecture of Erdős. The matching upper-bound construction (existence of graphs of girth r and m edges with max-cut at most m/2 + O(m^{r/(r+1)})) is known only for r = 4 and r = 5; the cases r ≥ 6 remain open according to subsequent surveys on graph partitions.

status_evidence.title: Better Bounds for Max Cut (Alon, Bollobás, Krivelevich, Sudakov / Bollobás-Scott)
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds of the form m/2 + c·m^{r/(r+1)} for max-cut in graphs of girth r, with optimality known in low-girth cases.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds matching the conjectured form are known; matching extremal constructions are established only for small r.

status_evidence.title: Maximum cuts and judicious partitions in graphs without short cycles
status_evidence.snippet: The order of the error term m^{r/(r+1)} is shown to be optimal for r=5, settling a special case of a conjecture of Erdős.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture verified for r=5 (and r=4); higher r open.
